Author: Sandeep Sharma
Bench: Sandeep Sharma
Vikas Vs. State of Hp .
Cr. Mp(M) No. 71 of 2024 13.08.2024 Present: Mr. George, Advocate, for the petitioner.

Mr. Rajan Kahol, Mr. Vishal Panwar & Mr. B.C Verma, Additional Advocate Generals with Mr. Ravi
Chauhan, Deputy Advocate General, for the respondent-State.
Cr. Mp(M) No. 71 of 2024 appellant for

By way of instant application filed under Section 5 of Limitation Act, prayer has been made on behalf of applicant- condonation of delay in maintaining the accompanying appeal, which is barred by limitation.

Pursuant to notices issued in the   application, respondent-State has filed reply, wherein prayer made on behalf of applicant-appellant for condonation of delay has been opposed on the ground that no plausible explanation has been rendered on record qua inordinate delay in maintaining accompanying appeal, which is barred by limitation.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and perused material available on record, this Court finds that vide judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 30.12.2022 passed by learned Additional District & Sessions Judge, Fast Track, Special Court (POCSO), District Shimla, appellant herein came to be convicted and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of seven years for his having committed offence punishable under Section 376 of IPC.

sentences.text: After having discovered factum with regard to non-filing of appeal, applicant-appellant engaged new counsel and requested him to file appeal before the Court against the judgment of conviction and order of sentence.

Counsel engaged by the applicant-appellant thereafter, applied for certified copy of judgment of conviction and order of sentence, which came to be supplied on 21.12.2023 and thereafter in the first week of January, 2024 accompanying appeal came to be filed.

Though this Court is persuaded to agree with Mr. Rajan Kahol, learned Additional Advocate General, that plausible explanation qua inordinate delay in maintaining the accompanying appeal has not been rendered on record, but this Court cannot lose sight of the fact that immediately after passing of judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 30.12.2022, applicant-appellant was taken into custody and thereafter, he was wholly dependent upon the counsel, who had represented him in the trial.

Otherwise also, .
applicant-appellant being in judicial lock up could not be expected to know the status of appeal, if any, filed on his behalf, rather he remained under bona fide belief that appeal filed on his behalf would be accepted and he would be acquitted.

Leaving everything aside, it is not in dispute that first appeal can be filed as a matter of right and in case, such right is denied on technical grounds, very purpose of providing opportunity to the applicant-appellant of filing appeal against the judgment of conviction and order of sentence would be defeated.

Since on account of judgment of conviction and order of sentence recorded by the learned Court below, liberty and freedom of the applicant-appellant is at stake, denying him right to file appeal, that too on the grounds of limitation, would otherwise amount to infraction of Article 21 of the Constitution of India.

In this regard reliance is placed upon the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Abdul Gafur Vs. State of Bihar & Ors., Criminal Appeal No. 1812 of 2011 arising out of the SLP Criminal No. 10358 of 2010, wherein Hon'ble Apex Court held that though law of limitation must even get due respect and observance by all the Courts, but in cases of conviction and imposition of sentence of imprisonment, the Court must show far greater indulgence and flexibility in applying the law of limitation than in any other kind of case.

entities.text: Abdul Gafur Vs. State of Bihar & Ors., Criminal Appeal No. 1812 of 2011
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hon'ble Apex Court held that a sentence of imprisonment relates to a person's right to personal liberty, which is one of the .
most important rights available to an individual and therefore, Court should be very reluctant to shut out a consideration of the case on the merits on grounds of limitation and any other similar technicality, rather all efforts should be made to decide the appeal on its own merits.

Relevant paras of the aforesaid judgment read as under:-
"The law of limitation is indeed an important law on the statute book.
It is in furtherance of the sound public policy to put a quietus to disputes or grievances of which resolution and redressal are not sought within the prescribed time.

The law of Vikas vs . State Of Hp on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196191429/
2 limitation is intended to allow things to finally settle down after a reasonable time and not to let everyone live in a state of uncertainty.

It does not permit any one to raise claims that are very old and stale and does not allow anyone to approach the higher tiers of the judicial system for correction of the lower court's orders or for redressal of grievances at ones own sweet will.
The law of limitation indeed must get due respect and observance by all courts.

We must, however, add that in cases of conviction and imposition of sentence of imprisonment, the court must show far greater indulgence and flexibility in applying the law of limitation than in any other kind of case.

A sentence of imprisonment relates to a person's right to personal liberty which is one of the most important rights available to an individual and,
therefore, the court should be very reluctant to shut out a consideration of the case on merits on grounds of limitation or any other similar technicality.
Coming to the case in hand, it is a well known fact that a large number of people come from Bihar to Delhi leaving their hearths and homes to earn a livelihood.
A vast number of them work in unorganized sectors.

Once caught in the vortex of earning the daily bread, all other important things in life such as marriage in the family,
medical treatment and even defending oneself in a criminal proceeding are relegated to the background.
We feel that the High Court dismissed the appellant's revision quite mechanically applying the bar of limitation and without giving any allowance to the circumstances of the appellants.

Looking at the matter from another point of view, under the .
Patna High Court Rules, a revision against conviction can be entertained only after the revision-petitioner surrenders before the court below.

Thankfully, this rule,
unlike some other provisions of the High Court Rules, is still followed very strictly.
Thus, as the revision filed by the appellants was taken up by the High Court they were already in jail.
In case, the revision was dismissed after consideration on merits, the appellants would have continued to remain in jail to serve out their sentences.
Had the revision been filed in time, they would have surrendered 15 months earlier and thus would have completed their sentence 15 months earlier.
All that happened due to the delayed filing of the revision is that they would complete their sentence, in case of dismissal of the revision 15 months later.

In light of what is said above, we are clearly of the view that it was a fit case in which the High Court should have condoned the delay in filing the revision by the appellants and examined their case on merits."
Reliance is also placed upon judgment passed by High Court of Delhi in Farhan Shaikh Vs. State (National Investigation Agency) AIRONLINE 2019 DEL 1156, (2019) 262 DLT 608.

sentences.text: The appellant seeks condonation of 314 days delay in filing the appeal.
The appellant seeks further delay of 44 days in re-filing the appeal.
The appeal, itself, is directed against the order on sentence.
Pertinently, the appellant was incarcerated when he was sentenced by the Special NIA Court.
In that situation, he was heavily dependent on his family and friends to file his appeal.
The appellant has explained that when he learnt of the sentence pronounced against him, he went into depression for about 6 months Thereafter, he started exploring avenues available to him.
He states that he attempted to consult a lawyer but he did not have the relevant documents.
He was confined in high security section of the jail and, consequently, it was difficult for him to arrange the documents.

Then his uncle .
from Maharashtra assured him of help.
His uncle contacted an NGO who, in turn, put him in touch with Mr. Aditya Wadhwa, Advocate.
He also explains that, in the meantime, the special NIA Court was shifted, which also delayed the procurement of documents.
93. We ask ourselves, what is the advantage to be gained by the appellant in delaying the filing of the appeal?
At the same time, what is the prejudice suffered by the State on account of this delayed filing of the appeal?
The answer to both these questions is "None".
The delay in filing the appeal is not so grave that the respondents could claim that it has destroyed its r record.
That is not even a plea taken by the respondent.
It is the appellant, who continues to suffer incarceration.
Therefore, it is he, who has suffered prejudice on account of his own delay.
The respondent has not suffered any prejudice due to the said delay."

Consequently, in view of facts as taken note hereinabove as well as law taken into consideration, this Court is convinced and satisfied and delay in maintaining the accompanying appeal is neither intentional nor willful, rather same has occurred on account of circumstances, which were completely beyond the control of the applicant and as such, same deserves to be condoned.
In view of above, delay of 360 days, which has been otherwise sufficiently explained is condoned.
The application is disposed of.
Appeal be registered.
Cr.Appeal No. _________ of 2024 (Cr.AST/114124) Admit.
Notice.

Mr. Rajan Kahol, learned Additional .
Advocate General, appears and waives service of notice on behalf of respondent.

Vikas vs . State Of Hp on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196191429/
4
Since pleadings are complete and parties are duly represented, let the appeal at hand be listed for consideration on 16.09.2024, as jointly agreed inter se parties.
In the meanwhile, record be called for.
This is an application for suspension of sentence.
It has been submitted by the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the applicant/appellant that the applicant/appellant was on bail during trial.
The appeal has been admitted.
There are arguable points in the appeal.
The hearing of the appeal will take some time.

In these circumstances, the substantive sentence of the applicant is suspended, and he is ordered to be enlarged on bail subject to depositing the entire fine amount, if not already deposited, within a period of four weeks and furnishing personal bonds in the sum of Rs.25,000/- with one surety in the like amount, to the satisfaction of the trial Court, within the same period with the condition that the applicant shall appear in Court, as and when directed and shall surrender to serve out the sentence imposed, in case the appeal is ultimately dismissed.
The application stands disposed of.
